answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed hillside tea-house that opens only on clear nights: the host serves saffron tea, points guests to one named nebula through a shared telescope, and keeps the mountain path lit by hand-carried lanterns, with every evening logged by the tourism authority. One host cannot run two tea-houses on the same night, and the license fee in outside money doubles per further tea-house on the same funding trail, so each extra fake identity costs another real tea-house, another live host, another season of clear-night service, and twice the prior fee.
